summary.title: Write your own Excel in 100 lines of F#
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small browser-based spreadsheet in F# using Fable, the Elmish architecture, and a hand-written parser combinator library.
keywords: how to build a spreadsheet in a browser
takeaways: Model a spreadsheet domain with F# types: Position, a recursive Expr discriminated union, and a Sheet map of raw inputs.
Build a UI with Elmish by defining State and Event types plus update and view functions, with React diffing the DOM.
Evaluate formulas recursively with pattern matching, using the option type and Option.bind to handle errors and detect recursive references.
Write a small parser combinator library (<*>, <|>, map, slot) to parse formulas into Expr values.
summary.summary: The author, who teaches F# FastTrack courses, walks through a simple Excel-like spreadsheet compiled to JavaScript with Fable. The post starts with a domain model (Position, a recursive Expr union, and Sheet), then builds the UI with Elmish, covering State, Event, update and a React-based view. The spreadsheet logic is covered next: formula evaluation with option-based error handling and recursion checks, followed by a small parser combinator library for formulas. The full source is in the elmish-spreadsheet GitHub repo, with a hands-on branch and a completed branch.
